headline: Finishing a Basement: Key Questions to Ask Before Choosing a Builder
articleBody:
Finishing lower-level living space adds square footage for guest bedrooms, recreation rooms, or home offices. Here is what to know before moving forward.

Key Benefits
A finished basement unlocks usable square footage without altering your home’s exterior footprint, giving your family flexible living space, an extra bathroom, or dedicated storage.

Process Breakdown
Every project should begin with foundation and moisture assessments. Sealing foundation cracks, addressing site drainage, and checking for radon or hazardous materials come before anything else. Once dry, framing, rough electrical, plumbing for future bathrooms, insulation, and fire blocking are installed. Only after trade inspections pass should drywall, flooring, trim carpentry, and paint proceed.

Real Examples
Transforming an unfinished concrete basement into a living suite requires proper framing setbacks, insulating concrete perimeter walls, and confirming emergency egress windows exist before framing a legal bedroom.

What to Prepare Before You Start
Check the clear height beneath ductwork and main beams, inspect your concrete slab for seasonal dampness, and map out where you need mechanical access panels.
